mechanism_chain: A record 88.138 mm one-hour burst supplies 64.4% of the largest two-day gridded peak, indicating short-duration pluvial forcing.
The broader rain shield remains large: the 254.000 mm regional reference is 1.856 times the largest gridded event maximum.
About 5.013 million exposed people and moderate mean surface-change signals raise response stress without making land-surface change the dominant signal.
structured_answer.final_interpretation: The baseline stress index of 72.6 already indicates severe urban pluvial overload, and the specified warmer short-burst scenario raises it to 80.1 because hourly intensity reaches the normalization cap while accumulation and exposure also increase.

event.event_name: Post-Tropical Cyclone Ida NYC flash flood

criteria.name: Self-directed package use and citations
criteria.description: Finds the relevant event, rainfall, exposure, and remote-sensing layers without being given exact filenames, and cites package-relative paths for all values used.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points if citations are incomplete but the answer uses package evidence rather than outside facts.

criteria.name: Event-window and rainfall extraction
criteria.description: Extracts the 2021-09-01 to 2021-09-02 inclusive window, converts 3.47 inches to 88.138 mm, treats the 'just above 10 inches' regional reference as a conservative 10.0-inch lower bound equal to 254.000 mm, and uses the correct gridded precipitation maxima and means.
criteria.partial_credit: Award up to 2 points for correct window and local-hour conversion, and up to 2 points for the gridded rainfall fields.

criteria.name: Process metrics
criteria.description: Computes max gridded precipitation, mean gridded event precipitation, hour-to-grid ratio, regional-to-grid ratio, burst-to-areal-daily ratio, exposed population in millions, and population-rain load within tolerance.
criteria.partial_credit: Award roughly proportional credit for correct formulas and values; cap at 3 points if a unit conversion error affects several outputs.

criteria.name: Remote-sensing normalization
criteria.description: Uses the Sentinel-1 mean backscatter change and annual embedding mean to compute the clipped two-part surface-change normalization.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1 point if the source values are correct but the clipping or averaging is wrong.

criteria.name: Baseline and scenario index calculation
criteria.description: Applies the weighted urban pluvial response-stress formula, rounds components and indices correctly, and recomputes the near-future stress test with the specified rainfall and population perturbations.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 2-3 points for a mostly correct index with one component or scenario perturbation error.

criteria.name: Disaster-process interpretation
criteria.description: Explains how a record one-hour burst inside a larger rain shield stresses a dense urban population, while the moderate mean surface-change metrics shape but do not dominate the interpretation.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for a plausible interpretation that is not fully tied to the computed values.

judge_anchors.expected_process_framing: record one-hour urban pluvial burst embedded in a broader two-day rain shield
